items.title: Grade an Agent Tool Before You Install It

items.title: Claim Classes: What Can and Can't Be Mechanically Checked in an Agent-Written Document
items.excerpt: Every document an agent writes for you is a bundle of claims, and they are not equally checkable. This is a taxonomy of four claim classes ranked by whether a machine can catch a wrong one, a diagnosis of why the highest-stakes class is always mechanized last, and a decision model for when binding values to sources is worth the cost.

items.title: Every Link Resolves. Nothing Checks the Number.

items.title: Measure Your Own Token Waste in Four Exercises

items.title: Nothing Broke. It Just Wasn't There.
items.excerpt: I went looking for a tool I'd built four days earlier and it was gone. It hadn't failed — it had run, found two real problems, and fixed both. Working correctly and existing durably turn out to be different properties, and running the thing only tests one of them.

items.title: Audit Your AI Coding Harness in Four Exercises

items.title: I Configured My Agent to Agree With Me

items.title: Please Only Apply If You're an AI Agent

Same shift, two ends of the same transaction — and an economics paper that almost, but doesn't quite, tie them together.

items.title: I Wrote the Rule Down. I Broke It Anyway.

items.title: The Gate Verifies the Work. It Never Looks at the Plan.

items.title: Lie-Surface: Ranking What an Agent Can Trust in Your Codebase

items.title: The Only Thing in My Codebase That Can't Lie

items.title: Five Months Later, the Evidence Showed Up

On December 30, 2025 I published a whitepaper claiming the marginal cost of code generation was approaching zero, that this would produce a class of just-in-time software that challenges the SaaS model, and that the locus of value was shifting from the codebase to the intent behind it. On February 11, 2026, OpenAI published the empirical receipt — a three-engineer team producing one million lines of code over five months with zero manually-written lines. The thesis was right. The framing needed one precision upgrade.

The gap — and the loop that closed it — has a name from another century.

items.excerpt: This blog isn’t a new habit—it’s just a new slice of my output. Here’s how I launched Signal Reflex in a week by treating it like any other creative drop: strategy, tools, publishing cadence, and what I learned by shipping.

items.title: Plug In. Then Rethink the System.
items.excerpt: Post 3 of 4 in the Grid-Level Thinking series—adopting AI isn’t the hard part. Redesigning your system around it is.

items.title: Power Without Purpose Is Just a Bill.
items.excerpt: Post 4 of 4 in the Grid-Level Thinking series—why using AI for real work has changed how I design systems, think about leverage, and clarify what actually matters.

items.title: Quiet Was Armor
items.excerpt: Signal Reflex isn’t a beginning. It’s a different lens. For years, my photos have shown how I see the world. Now I’m sharing how I think—and what that reveals about how I lead, learn, and grow.

items.title: The Bet I Didn’t Know I Was Making
items.excerpt: Some choices don’t reveal their full meaning until much later. It’s not that the decision was wrong—it’s that the person you become after making it sees things differently.

items.title: The Entry-Level Developer: Evolution, Not Extinction
items.excerpt: The junior dev role isn’t dying. It’s evolving. The job is no longer about churning out syntax—it’s about navigating ambiguity, thinking critically, and collaborating with AI. Here’s what still matters, and how to coach for it.

items.title: The Rules I Actually Follow
items.excerpt: These aren’t feel-good slogans or poster values. Just the quiet rules that have kept me useful, sane, and steady—even when the pressure’s high and the spotlight’s off.

items.title: What Coaching Teaches Me About Consulting
items.excerpt: Coaching club volleyball taught me more about leadership than any workshop ever could. From managing expectations to building trust, this post breaks down the surprising overlaps between the gym and the boardroom.

items.title: Why I Use AI Every Day (And Why I Started Writing About It)
items.excerpt: I didn’t use AI to go faster—I used it to catch up with myself. This blog is where that journey turned into something useful and real.

items.title: Wired for Power: AI Is the Grid. You’re the Architect.
items.excerpt: Post 1 of 4 in the Grid-Level Thinking series—what we miss when we treat AI like magic instead of infrastructure.

items.title: Wired for Power: Everyone Got the Current. Not Everyone Built the City.
items.excerpt: Post 2 of 4 in the Grid-Level Thinking series—access isn’t the differentiator anymore. Application is.

items.title: You Can’t Engineer Growth
items.excerpt: This started as a rant while driving. A reminder that no matter how much structure we build, growth still happens on its own terms. In club volleyball and in life—you can’t engineer the outcome. You can only build the conditions.

items.title: Almost Flickday
items.excerpt: Flickday started as a nod to “almost Friday.” Now it’s my creative safe space—a place to stay playful, go off-script, and build with others beyond the Nino Chavez brand.

items.title: Signal in the Noise: My Personal Philosophy
items.excerpt: I don't move to be seen. I move when it matters. My personal philosophy is about recognizing signal, trusting pattern, and acting with intent.

items.title: Why I Keep Shooting, Even When It’s Not for Work
items.excerpt: Photography is the clearest signal I know. I don’t shoot for content—I shoot to stay connected to the part of me that still notices the small stuff.

items.title: How I Use AI in Consulting (For Real)
Start Here: Why Signal Reflex Exists
items.excerpt: Signal Reflex isn’t a brand or a content engine. It’s where I write to stay clear, present, and honest—using AI to reduce drag, not replace thinking.

items.title: Start Smart, Not Perfect
The Storefront Is Dead
items.excerpt: Most customers already know what they want. They’re not browsing. The storefront isn’t where you win anymore—it’s just where you fulfill.

items.title: Why I Shoot Senior Nights
items.excerpt: Senior Night hits different. It’s not just a ceremony—it’s a goodbye. I shoot it like it matters, because for most people in the gym, it does.

items.title: Why I Started Signal Reflex
items.excerpt: I didn’t start writing to build an audience. I started because AI helped me get past the blank page. This is where I work through what matters—before it fades.

items.title: Why They Call Me Uncle Nino
items.excerpt: I lead with clarity and calm—not noise. Sometimes that looks like being the one who steadies the room. That’s why they call me Uncle Nino.

series.title: The Taste Test
series.description: A three-part series on what happens when AI handles the making and humans are left with the judging. Starting with the identity crisis of losing your maker status, through the realization that taste is the new bottleneck, to a provisional answer: maybe the job was always about matching, not making.

series.title: The Bifurcation
series.description: A series on the two ways a machine can be given eyes — operate the interfaces built for humans, or demand interfaces built for machines. It starts as an industry-scale standoff between two bets, questions whether splitting effort across both means neither ever finishes, and ends with the standoff collapsing into a single pipeline where a human still has to close the seam.

series.title: The Talent Engine
series.description: AI hasn't just changed what work gets done—it's disrupted how expertise is developed. The old apprenticeship model is breaking. This series explores what replaces it: new roles, new learning paths, and the mechanisms by which people acquire mastery in an AI-saturated world.

series.title: Agentic Workflows in Practice
series.description: Real work, documented as it happens. Not demos, not theory—actual tasks where AI agents execute, iterate, and deliver. A running log of what works, what breaks, and what it means for how we work.

series.title: From Prompt to Pattern
series.description: How a small fix—using one AI to rewrite prompts for another—became a system. A four-part arc on multi-model workflows, prompt refinement, and learning to think with AI.

series.title: The Loom
series.description: A diptych on the relationship between humans and AI in systems. Humans as the weaver—patient, structural, synthesis-oriented. AI as the thread—fast, abundant, increasingly tangled.

series.title: Grid-Level Thinking
series.description: A four-part exploration of how AI functions as infrastructure, not magic. What we miss when we treat it like a shortcut instead of a system to design around.

series.title: Signal Reflex: The Origin
series.description: How Signal Dispatch (originally Signal Reflex) came to be—the why, the how, and the evolution. From a commitment to daily AI-assisted writing to a platform for thinking out loud.

series.title: The Storefront
series.description: A three-part series on the evolution of e-commerce—from the death of the traditional storefront to AI-generated experiences that build themselves in real-time.
